title: Xanthe and the Deadline
premise: Noor Quintana, a disgraced intelligence analyst on her last chance, discovers that a decommissioned safe house she once ran has been listed online — interior photos revealing documents, layouts, and one hidden ledger that could expose a fifteen-year-old sanctioned operation. The listing is bait, set by someone inside her old network who needs Noor to surface so they can pin the leak on her. As she races to retrieve the ledger before the sale closes, she must decide whether to trade it to a hostile broker or burn it and destroy the man who trained her — and the lover who betrayed her. In the end, Noor chooses truth over loyalty, testifying at cost of her career, and walks away free but unemployable, finally her own.
about_author: Petra Oyelaran is a former compliance consultant who spent a decade auditing the paper trails of institutions that preferred to stay invisible. She writes thrillers about people who read the fine print too late.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., she recognizes the safe house from her first posting — and in photo seven, the edge of a document case she buried there years ago. The emotional beat: cold dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Three Strikes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how she was bounced from three agencies, each exit tied to following rules no one else followed. Her current handler, Voss, summons her; someone flagged the listing internally. Beat: humiliation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Posing as a buyer, she tours the house and finds the hiding spot empty — but fresh tool marks mean someone got there first. A realtor mentions an earlier visitor with a government lanyard. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Voss reports to Director Hale that the ledger is missing, concealing his own role in the original operation. Beat: the reader learns Voss is lying before Noor does.

chapters.title: The Man Who Trained Me
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She tracks down Elias Brandt, her old mentor, now retired and charmingly evasive. He warns her off, then slips her a burner number. Beat: warmth undercut by the sense she's being managed.

chapters.title: Broker's Terms
chapters.summary: Kaspar Rehn's POV. The hostile broker who actually holds the ledger sets terms: he'll sell it back to the agency unless Noor delivers something better — the name of the operation's authorizing officer. Beat: predatory patience.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Reconstructing the original op from memory and redacted files, she realizes the ledger implicates Hale himself. Beat: the vertigo of discovering the rules were always someone else's weapon.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, tense chase chapter. She spots surveillance outside her flat and runs a counter-surveillance route through the city, losing them by inches — or letting herself be lost. Beat: adrenaline and self-doubt.

chapters.title: The Lover's Alibi
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Tomas Reyes, her ex-partner and former lover, now at another agency, feeding her information while reporting fragments to Hale. Beat: tenderness braided with betrayal the reader can see coming.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A planned exchange with Brandt goes wrong; she finds his contact dead and a message meant for her: 'They know you know.' Beat: grief converting fear into anger.

chapters.title: Hale's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Director Hale's POV. He offers Noor reinstatement if she surrenders whatever she finds and names Rehn as the leak. Beat: the seduction of legitimacy offered by the guilty.

chapters.title: What the Photos Sold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Forensic work on the listing reveals it was posted from an agency-adjacent server — the bait was internal. Someone wanted her flushed into the open. Beat: betrayal narrowing to a shortlist.

chapters.title: Rehn's Price
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. He raises stakes: auction deadline moved up to forty-eight hours, buyers including a foreign service. Beat: clock tightening, moral ground eroding under everyone.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Ordered to deliver Noor, he instead burns his own cover partially to buy her time, knowing it ends his career either way. Beat: love choosing a side it can't take back.

chapters.title: The Safe House Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She breaks into the listed house at night to search for a duplicate cache and finds Voss waiting — gun drawn, confession half-offered, half-threatened. Beat: the past holding her at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Negotiation in the Dark
chapters.summary: Noor and Voss's POV alternating within the standoff. Voss admits the op was sanctioned off-book by Hale; he wants the ledger destroyed to protect them both. Beat: complicity offered as mercy.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With the auction looming, she copies the ledger, sends one set to a journalist, and prepares to meet Rehn with a forged version. Beat: cold clarity — she stops asking permission.

chapters.title: The Auction Room
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV climax build. Buyers assemble; Noor arrives as an unexpected bidder with her forgery, forcing Rehn to authenticate against a ticking window. Beat: high-wire tension.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The exchange detonates: Hale's team raids, Rehn is taken, but Noor slips the true ledger's existence into the record via the journalist's confirmation call. Beat: victory that feels like falling.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Confronting Hale with evidence, she refuses his final offer of silence-for-survival. Tomas arrives as her witness, burning his last bridge beside her. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The inquiry chapters close: Hale falls, Voss takes a reduced fall, Noor is cleared and simultaneously blacklisted. Beat: justice delivered without redemption.

chapters.title: Sold Sign
chapters.summary: Noor's POV epilogue. The safe house finally sells; she watches the new owners move in, keeps nothing but a photograph of the listing itself. Free, unemployable, and for the first time honest. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
